edge.rationale: Two-digit place value practises treating ten ones as one ten.
Bundling ten ones is a core representation of two-digit place value.
Interpreting tens and ones is central to two-digit place value.
Base-ten blocks are a common model for two-digit place value.
Composing numbers from tens and ones is direct practice of two-digit place value.
Decomposing numbers into tens and ones is direct practice of two-digit place value.
Reading and writing two-digit numerals applies tens-and-ones meaning to notation.
Expanded form makes the value of each two-digit place explicit.
Comparing two-digit numbers uses the place-value structure of tens and ones.
Three-digit place value practises treating ten tens as one hundred.
Interpreting hundreds, tens and ones is central to three-digit place value.
Base-ten blocks are a common model for three-digit place value.
Composing from hundreds, tens and ones directly practises three-digit place value.
Decomposing into hundreds, tens and ones directly practises three-digit place value.
Reading and writing three-digit numerals applies hundreds-tens-ones meaning to notation.
Expanded form makes the value of each three-digit place explicit.
Treating ten ones as one ten depends on being able to count out a target quantity of ten.
edge.failure_signal: Learner cannot reliably form a group of ten before naming it as one ten.

edge.rationale: Bundling ten ones depends on knowing that ten ones can be treated as one ten.
edge.failure_signal: Learner makes groups but cannot explain why a group of ten is one ten.

edge.rationale: Interpreting tens and ones depends on the unit of ten formed by bundling ones.
edge.failure_signal: Learner reads digits separately without interpreting tens as groups of ten.

edge.rationale: Base-ten models require interpreting rods as tens and units as ones.
edge.failure_signal: Learner counts every unit individually and does not use rods as tens.

edge.rationale: Composing two-digit numbers requires knowing the tens and ones places.
edge.failure_signal: Learner cannot build a two-digit number from specified tens and ones.

edge.rationale: Decomposing reverses the process of composing numbers from tens and ones.
edge.failure_signal: Learner cannot break a two-digit number into tens and ones.

edge.rationale: Reading and writing two-digit numerals depends on connecting places to tens and ones.
edge.failure_signal: Learner writes digits in the wrong order or reads each digit as a separate number.

edge.rationale: Expanded form requires decomposing a number into its place values.
edge.failure_signal: Learner writes a digit sum rather than a place-value decomposition.

edge.rationale: Comparing two-digit numbers depends on interpreting tens before ones.
edge.failure_signal: Learner compares only the ones digit or treats digits independently.

edge.rationale: One hundred is built from ten tens, so it depends on understanding tens as units.
edge.failure_signal: Learner cannot explain a hundred as ten groups of ten.

edge.rationale: Interpreting hundreds, tens and ones depends on recognising one hundred as a unit.
edge.failure_signal: Learner reads the hundreds digit without relating it to hundreds units.

edge.rationale: Base-ten models require interpreting flats as hundreds, rods as tens and units as ones.
edge.failure_signal: Learner does not distinguish hundreds, tens and ones models.

edge.rationale: Composing three-digit numbers requires knowing hundreds, tens and ones places.
edge.failure_signal: Learner cannot build a three-digit number from specified place-value parts.

edge.rationale: Decomposing reverses composing a number from hundreds, tens and ones.
edge.failure_signal: Learner cannot break a three-digit number into place-value parts.

edge.rationale: Reading and writing three-digit numerals depends on place-value meaning for each digit.
edge.failure_signal: Learner writes digits in the wrong places or omits zero placeholders.

edge.rationale: Expanded form requires decomposing a three-digit number into place values.
edge.failure_signal: Learner writes digit sums instead of hundreds, tens and ones values.
